intent: CF-V0-028: an independent consumer MUST reproduce every reference result byte-for-byte. The canonical vectors under vectors/ are that independent derivation, authored from the clause text and checked by the reference codec in refcodec.go, which shares no code with the implementation.

cases.note: vectors/codec.json and vectors/identity.json. The declared universe carries the CEM `unknown` hunk the expected item comes from, because CF-V0-009 conditions that item on such a hunk existing: `a CEM unknown hunk emits exactly one HUNK_BASIS item`, mapping `no-evidence -> HUNK_NO_EVIDENCE`. Nothing in CF-V0-028 or CF-V0-019 supplies a subject, so a case that named the item without declaring its hunk would be asking the runner to invent one. It cannot: a canonical patch is never empty, so a universe declaring no hunk gets a whitespace-only filler, which CF-V0-008 closes and which therefore emits no item at all.
assertions: CF-V0-019: the implementation's codec MUST agree byte-for-byte with every serialize vector.
CF-V0-019: the implementation MUST reject every invalid vector with the named reason.
CF-V0-006 / CF-V0-007: the implementation's universe and item IDs MUST equal the hand-derived identity vectors for the same preimage.
CF-V0-028: Corvint producer-to-Corvint verifier tests alone cannot satisfy this requirement, so these vectors are authored from the spec and never captured from a run.

CF-V0-009: the emitted item is the one this universe's CEM `unknown` hunk requires, not one the runner supplied; declaring the hunk is what makes the expectation derivable from the clause rather than from the implementation.
